title: Repurposing Monensin for Inflammation and Immunity: A Comprehensive Review
content: Monensin, a polyether ionophore antibiotic used extensively in veterinary medicine, has recently generated interest for its possible anti-inflammatory effects. Monensin has commonly been referred to as a coccidiostat and growth promoter used in livestock; however, monensin has significant effects on cellular ion homeostasis and intracellular signaling pathways, which may lead to clinically relevant immunomodulatory effects. Here, we will summarize the current knowledge regarding the anti-inflammatory mechanisms of monensin, including both in vitro and in vivo studies. Evidence indicates that monensin can inhibit nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB) activation, inhibit the phosphorylation of mitogen-activated protein kinases (MAPK), and inhibit TLR–mediated signaling, which is important for the reduction in pro-inflammatory cytokines such as TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6 expression. In animal models, monensin has been reported to improve survival during endotoxemia, improve microglial activation during neuroinflammatory conditions, or attenuate gut injury in models of colitis or arthritis. Monensin has also modulated tumor-associated inflammation, suggesting broader use of the drug in the field of oncology.Although these preliminary findings are encouraging, the limitations of safety, poor pharmacokinetics, and the limited use in veterinary medicine have restricted its translation to human medicine. Advances in delivery systems, structural analogues, and repurposing options have the potential to establish its therapeutic applicability. In summary, monensin presents as a promising albeit understudied candidate for anti-inflammatory therapy. There is a clearly defined need for further mechanistic studies, toxicological assessments, and translational research studies
